about: Skill-finding tasks (protocol v2, chapter 4, J1). Each task names a realistic piece of work; `gold` lists the skills that clearly apply, one group per skill (a group with two names: either one counts); `ok` lists skills that are reasonable but not required, so loading them is not counted as wrong. Fixed before any run.

tasks.task: Build a responsive landing page with a pricing section and a dark mode for my React web app, and finish it with my usual author footer.
Implement this Figma screen as a Vue component that matches our design, including its hover and entrance animations.
Build an MCP server in TypeScript that wraps our REST API, and package it so my colleagues can install it in Claude Desktop with one click.
Create a Claude Code plugin with a /deploy slash command, a PreToolUse hook that blocks force pushes, and a settings file the user can configure.
Our checkout API sometimes returns 500 under load and one of its tests is flaky. Find the cause, fix it, and prove that it is fixed.
My desktop app is finished. After a final code review, publish it to GitHub as a private portfolio repository with a proper README, screenshots and my namecard in the app.
Turn last quarter's sales CSV into an Excel workbook with charts, then a 10-slide PowerPoint summary of it and a PDF version for the board.
We need a new multi-tenant billing module. Brainstorm the design with me, write an implementation plan, then implement it with subagents in an isolated git worktree.
Write a new skill that teaches Claude our team's code review checklist, test whether it triggers on the right prompts, and tune its description.
Take our React component library and build a matching design system in Figma, with variables for the tokens and Code Connect mappings back to the code.
I just plugged in a new M5Stack Cardputer over USB. Set it up, then help me iterate on the Snake game app on it.
For my learning project, build a REST API with authentication and a database, and explain each step and decision as you go so that I understand it.
